record.paper_title: Structure and dynamics of reentrant nematics: Any open questions after almost 40 years?
record.context_brief: Nematic order across the SA-RN transition
record.original_question: How does the nematic orientational order parameter Q change when a liquid crystal crosses from a smectic-A (SA) phase, in which molecules organize in layers, into a reentrant nematic (RN) phase, and can experiments resolve whether Q increases sharply, changes only subtly, or shows no enhancement?

evidence.quote: The most commonly encountered phases are nematic (N), where the system has a preferential orientation given by the nematic director, but the centers of mass have no long-range correlation; smectic (S), where molecules organize in layers.
The structure of RN's also poses some unanswered questions. For example, is there a change in nematic order parameter Q at the transition from S to RN?
Nonetheless, the question still lingers: What is the behavior of the nematic order across the S-RN phase transition?
How does the nematic order change upon crossing the SA-RN transition?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a thermotropic liquid crystal that, upon cooling, exhibits the phase sequence nematic (N) → smectic-A (SA) → reentrant nematic (RN). In the nematic phases, rod-like molecules share a common preferential orientation (the director $\hat n$) but their centers of mass are positionally disordered; the degree of orientational alignment is quantified by the scalar nematic order parameter
$$Q \;=\; \bigl\langle P_2(\cos\theta)\bigr\rangle \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl\langle 3\cos^2\theta - 1\bigr\rangle,$$
where $\theta$ is the angle between a molecular long axis and $\hat n$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes a thermal/ensemble average. In the SA phase the molecules additionally form a one-dimensional density wave organized into layers perpendicular to $\hat n$.

Determine the behavior of the nematic orientational order parameter $Q(T)$ as the temperature $T$ is varied across the SA → RN phase transition. Specifically, decide which of the following holds, and justify by theory and/or experimentally resolvable measurement:

(i) $Q$ increases sharply (a discontinuous or pronounced jump) upon entering the RN phase from the SA phase;
(ii) $Q$ changes only subtly (a small, possibly continuous variation) across the transition;
(iii) $Q$ shows no enhancement, varying smoothly as if no transition occurred in the orientational order.

Provide the qualitative and, if possible, quantitative dependence of $Q$ on $T$ near the SA–RN boundary, and identify experimental observables (e.g., birefringence, Raman depolarization ratios, NMR splittings, X-ray-derived $\langle P_2\rangle$) capable of distinguishing these scenarios.
artifact.status_search_result: The behavior of the nematic order parameter Q across the smectic-A to reentrant-nematic transition is discussed in the liquid-crystal literature primarily through Landau-theory couplings between nematic and smectic order parameters (e.g., Cladis-type models and subsequent Landau analyses), but a definitive, experimentally resolved answer—whether Q jumps sharply, varies subtly, or shows no enhancement at the SA–RN boundary—does not appear to be settled. Surveys of reentrant nematics continue to list this as an open structural question.

status_evidence.title: Landau Theory of the Reentrant Nematic-Smectic A Phase Transition
status_evidence.snippet: The reentrant nematic to smectic A phase transition is shown to follow from Landau theory if one assumes an optimum density for smectic ordering.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical Landau-type frameworks exist but do not uniquely fix the magnitude of the change in Q across the SA-RN transition.

status_evidence.title: Critical behavior at nematic-to-smectic-A phase transitions for SmA1 and reentrant SmAd phases
status_evidence.snippet: Critical behavior at nematic-to-smectic-A phase transitions for SmA1 and reentrant SmAd phases.
status_evidence.claim: Critical behavior near these transitions has been studied but the nematic order parameter behavior across SA-RN remains discussed.

status_evidence.title: On the nematic, smectic, and reentrant nematic phase in cyanobiphenyls
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of nematic, smectic and reentrant nematic phases in cyanobiphenyl liquid crystals.
status_evidence.claim: The structural questions about reentrant nematics in canonical materials remain a topic of ongoing investigation.
